description: Measured 2026-08-17 by two audit passes that verified every claim against the real tree (imports executed in-process, make -qp target list, actual --help output). Scope is far larger than the CLI help defects tracked in fix-customer-facing-cli-url-and-help-defects. (1) Imports: 24 distinct failures out of 238 tested, so about 10 percent of documented Python imports do not work. Includes docs/guides/tpc/tpc-di-deployment-guide.md, whose entire parallel-execution section is built on three symbols (ParallelBenchmarkConfig, ParallelExecutionMode, ParallelWorkloadType) that do not exist. (2) CONTRIBUTING.md:226-231 documents a 4-step release flow in which all four make targets are fictional (make bump, changelog-draft, release-prepare, release-rebase-develop); the real flow is release-cut then release-finalize, and CONTRIBUTING.md links to the guide that says so while contradicting it. (3) README.md:759,854,903 tell users to run --describe-platform-options, an option that was removed - benchbox/cli/commands/run.py:591 hardcodes describe_platforms = () and the handler is dead code. (4) Roughly 150 CLI examples across docs/ would fail if typed: benchbox run given a nonexistent -o short flag in 23 places, benchbox run given a positional benchmark name it does not accept, renamed tuning subcommands, a benchbox credentials command that never existed, and per-platform flags like --warehouse, --staging-root, --datafusion-memory-limit and --lakesail-endpoint that were never CLI options and must be --platform-option KEY=VALUE. (5) Two docs describe whole surfaces that do not exist: benchbox admin (11 sites in docs/operations/results-phase-3-runbook.md plus docs/reference/threat-model.md) and benchbox explorer build (9 sites in an Accepted ADR). This is the highest-frequency way a new user meets a broken product: the platform docs for Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery and Databricks all instruct users to pass flags that do not parse.
